analysis.title: SpaceX catches Starship Flight 15, data centers and space contracts are renewed focus post-midterms
key_insights: SpaceX (SPCX) completed its first upper-stage Starship catch with Flight 15 from Starbase, TX. RBC sees it as a key step toward Starship reusability and future launch cadence, and a de-risking of cost reductions across Connectivity and AI.

The Super Heavy booster exploded in the gulf after diverting from a tower catch. SPCX said the diversion was correct, with early indications of low fuel on re-entry. RBC does not see it as a significant sentiment risk because SPCX has caught the booster before.

SPCX plans two supercompute facilities, one in Rio Grande Valley, TX (>$24B plus $220M for Brownsville water and wastewater infrastructure) and one in Cochise County, AZ (~$50B), for a combined >$74B. The Texas site is planned to generate its own electricity without drawing on the public grid.

RBC sees more headline risk for terrestrial data center construction after the midterms. It expects the build to continue, perhaps at a slower pace, and says the shifting political landscape increases the focus on space-based compute.

RBC expects Democrats could pressure SPCX's NASA-related contracts to strengthen competition and make awards less politically biased. It still sees SPCX as best-positioned in the space sector and says the government has no real alternative to SPCX's lift capacity.
NASA unveiled a $10B Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) framework that RBC says may drive incremental SPCX bookings, helped by the failed ULA Vulcan launch.

RBC maintains Outperform and a $225 price target against a $139.11 price. The target applies a weighted average 10x EV/EBITDA multiple to FY29 SOTP adj. EBITDA of $280.2B (15x Space, 9.5x Connectivity, 10x AI).
Scenario values are $275 upside (faster Starship cadence, ~$424B sales, ~$297B EBITDA, 11.5x) and $100 downside (slower cadence, ~$218B revenue, ~$135.6B EBITDA, 9x).

RBC estimates revenue of $51.4B in 2026E, $218.4B in 2027E and $344.5B in 2028E, and adj. EBITDA of $27.1B, $133.5B and $224.7B. 2025A revenue was $18.7B and adj. EBITDA $6.6B. Q3 2026 revenue was $14.6B and adj. EBITDA $8.8B.
RBC models free cash flow of -$60.6B in 2026E and -$48.3B in 2027E, turning positive in 2030E at $20.2B. Capex is $84.6B in 2026E rising to $160.2B in 2027E.
RBC says investors remain focused on a potential merger with Tesla (TSLA).

Starship launch cadence is the foundational question for the thesis. The company's framework needs 3,500-7,800 cumulative Starship launches to reach 50 GW of orbital compute, which RBC calls ambitious but achievable. RBC calls sustained cadence improvement post-2028 the most important stock catalyst.

Connectivity: Starlink's ~5-year satellite replacement cycle is a capex burden versus fiber and cable assets with 15-25-year lives. RBC says V3 satellite cost cuts, CPE subsidies and Government & Enterprise mix can improve gross margins. RBC prefers an MVNO route over building a fourth wireless network for Mobility.

AI: RBC sees cheaper open-source models as an accelerant for compute demand (OpenRouter tokens grew from 6.5T to 44T a month in nine months). Grok's intelligence index is 38 versus a market-leading 60, and the $60B Cursor acquisition is pending close.
Musk holds ~82.3% of voting power, making SPCX a controlled company. This is a governance risk for Class A holders.

market_movers.rationale: The first Starship upper-stage catch de-risks reusability and the Connectivity and AI cost case. Data center and NASA-contract political headline risk is a watch item.

sector_views.rationale: RBC sees SPCX as best-positioned across the space sector, with the government lacking real alternatives to its lift capacity.

earnings_insights: RBC estimates 2026E revenue of $51,411.2M and adj. EBITDA of $27,108.8M (RBC estimates, not reported).
Reported 2026 quarters: Q1 revenue $4,694M, Q2 $7,814M, Q3 $14,575M. Adj. EBITDA Q1 $1,127M, Q2 $3,538M, Q3 $8,809M. RBC estimates Q4 2026 revenue of $24,328.2M and adj. EBITDA of $13,593M.
RBC estimates 2027E revenue of $218,373.4M and adj. EBITDA of $133,453.0M. Adj. diluted EPS estimates are $1.16 for 2026E and $8.54 for 2027E (RBC estimates, non-GAAP).
RBC estimates FY29 adj. EBITDA of $280,207M on $410,032M of revenue. Segment FY29E revenue is Space $9,269M, Connectivity $78,339M and AI $322,425M.
risk_factors: Starship development delays or failures could impair the launch, Connectivity and AI growth strategies.
Launch failures, operational hazards and uninsured asset losses.
Regulatory and licensing risk from FAA, FCC or international licenses.
Orbital debris and LEO congestion risk to satellites and launch vehicles.
The xAI segment is early-stage, loss-generating and subject to integration risk.
Key person dependency on Elon Musk, who holds ~82% of voting power.
Heavy ongoing capital needs for power, GPUs and data centers, with free cash flow negative through 2029E.
Political and headline risk to terrestrial data center construction and NASA contracts after the midterms.
geopolitical: RBC expects post-midterm Democratic pressure on SPCX's NASA-related contracts and on data center construction.
NASA unveiled a $10B Commercial Lunar Payload Services framework.

tension_points.bull_case: RBC says the terrestrial data center build will continue, and the focus on energy investment (self-generated power in Texas, up to 20% lower bills for Arizona cooperative members) helps win local approval.
tension_points.bear_case: RBC says the build may slow because of post-midterm political pushback and headline risk, similar to the pressure on SPCX's NASA contracts.

theme_stances.key_argument: The first upper-stage catch de-risks the reusability case that enables cost reductions across Connectivity and AI.
Democrats could pressure NASA contracts and data center construction, though the government has no real alternative to SPCX's lift capacity.
